chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

It is written in the Torah which has not been altered that Musa (peace be upon him) asked his Lord (may He be exalted) saying: 'My God! A situation comes upon me such that it would not be honourable and majestic for You that I should mention You therein'. So He said: 'O Musa! My Mention is good upon every state'.
ai.seo_question: What did God say to Musa about remembering Him in all states?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (as) cites an unaltered portion of the Torah to affirm that divine remembrance is perpetually virtuous, countering concerns about context or state. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that dhikr is not merely a ritual but a continuous spiritual state, reinforcing the obligation of remembering Allah in every gathering as a fundamental aspect of worship.
